abandon: The mechanism says the base fails between problems because it settles on a length budget from the prompt that is too small, so it writes a short, compressed answer where RL writes a long one. The board items say the opposite: the base's failures are long answers, and its failures on one problem are sporadic, which a budget fixed by the prompt cannot produce. (1) result-5e17a6: 'Base answers <= 2,000 tokens: 263, 13 wrong'. Short base answers are about 95 % right, so at most 13 of the base's 63 finished-wrong MATH-500 answers can be short. Its hand labels of the 65 RL-only problems name '14 misread, 14 arithmetic/algebra slip' and '16 cap hits with no loop', and none is a truncated or compressed solution. (2) result-f21d2e: 'no J-lens feature predicts a wrong base answer better than length (AUROC length 0.831'. Together with (1) this means longer base answers are the wrong ones. Under the mechanism, base length would be a weak or reversed predictor of failure. (3) result-afc423: '81% of the 198-sample gap (4 samples per problem' lies in problems the base solves at least once, and 'Cell base 3/4 -> RL 4/4: 86 problems = 43% of the gap'. A budget fixed by the prompt is shared by every sample of a problem, so the right siblings show the budget was big enough. The facts entry for r5-m02 also shows the wrong siblings run longer (+0.19 log ratio), not shorter. At most the 19 % in base-0/4 problems is left for the mechanism. (4) result-a6ab7a: 'Base fails RL prefixes mostly by cap hit (34 of 48 wrong at 50 %)'. Even when RL's long plan is handed to it, the base fails by running past the cap, not by stopping early. (5) result-51fd20: 'its cap hits on the 328 are failures to solve, not failures to stop', and 'the tokens between 8,000 and 16,384 buy 12 problems'. The base loses problems when it is cut short and wins problems by writing long. (6) The observation the mechanism was built on does not support it. result-b30f15's probe at the last prompt token predicts 'sample is in the largest group of agreeing answers' across problems at 0.73-0.77. That is problem difficulty, which also drives length up, not a short length budget. The proposed first test conditions on finished answers in RL-length quartiles, but the items above already place the base's errors on its long answers, inside the same problems where shorter siblings succeed.
